President Bola Tinubu has expanded his campaign itinerary for the 2027 presidential election, increasing the number of states he plans to visit from 12 to 19, with the Federal Capital Territory also included. The PUNCH gathered that the revised timetable shows that Tinubu is expected to attend 20 rallies organised by the All Progressives Congress across the country between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027. President Tinubu had disclosed during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council on October 14 that he would be unable to attend all campaign rallies. The new additions to the itinerary include Katsina, Taraba, Zamfara, Imo and Kwara, while Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi have also been included following Tinubu’s recent campaign appearances in the states. Tinubu had already attended rallies in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on November 6; Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on November 7; Dutse, Jigawa State, on November 10; and Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, on November 17. Other engagements include Gusau, Zamfara State, on December 28, and Owerri, Imo State, on December 30. 2027: Adebayo promises N200 petrol, end Boko Haram No serious rift between Tinubu, Makinde – Oyo monarch 2027: Uzodimma backs Tinubu’s re-election, urges patience with reforms The President is also scheduled to resume campaigning in the New Year with rallies in Yola, Adamawa State, on January 4; Sokoto on January 5; and Ilorin, Kwara State, on January 8. He will subsequently visit Asaba, Delta State, on January 11, before concluding the campaign with a rally in Lagos on January 13. The APC calendar also features changes to the original timetable, including the postponement of the Sokoto rally from December 5 to January 5 and the movement of the Lagos campaign finale from January 9 to January 13. The revised campaign schedule places the North-West ahead of other geopolitical zones, with Tinubu expected to visit seven states: Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto. The North-East and South-South have three states each on the itinerary, while the North-Central, South-West and South-East have two states apiece.
